## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-generated branchless blend for the death/respawn step, combined with an optimized render pass, can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on this workload.

## Cache saturation
All measured N values (10000–10000000) lie past both the L1d spill (N≈481) and the L2 spill (N≈7710), so the curve starts already in the L3 regime. At q=0.01 the cost is essentially FLAT from N=10000 to N=100000 (19.824 → 19.683 ns/p), then RISES modestly at N=1000000 (21.547) as the working set crosses the L3 spill at N≈246723, before settling back to 20.562 at N=10000000. Death rate raises the floor monotonically without reshaping the N-curve: at N=100000, ns/p goes 19.683 (q=0.01) → 20.938 (q=0.1) → 22.895 (q=0.25) → 24.876 (q=0.5), a 26% spread. The L3→DRAM knee is real but mild (~9% at N=1M), and the dominant cost variation comes from death rate, not cache depth.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 3.45 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — only 27% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: backend_stall is 0.0% across every profile, while frontend_stall dominates at 48.4–52.7%. There is no transition to a bandwidth-bound regime at any N or death rate; bandwidth instead drifts downward with both increasing N (3.45 → 3.16 GB/s from N=100K to N=1M at q=0.01) and increasing death rate (3.45 → 2.72 GB/s from q=0.01 to q=0.5 at N=10000). The hypothesis's prediction of approaching the streaming ceiling is not met in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the particle loop — the histogram reports 0 vector-suffixed instructions, and all floating-point work is scalar: `vmulss` (4), `vaddss` (1), `vsubss` (1). The 14 `vmovaps` are confined to the prologue, zeroing stack scratch space after a `sub rsp,0x448` (1096-byte frame). The only packed operation on particle data is `vpaddusb` (2), performing byte-granular saturating adds for the RGBA blend. The scatter is scalar byte stores: `mov BYTE PTR [r13+rdi*1+0x0]` repeated for each of R, G, B, plus a `mov BYTE PTR ...,0xff` for the alpha channel. The 379-instruction body with extensive stack setup (`mov QWORD PTR [rbp-...]` dominating the histogram at 153 `mov` + 45 `lea`) explains the 48–53% frontend stalls — the decode pipeline cannot sustain throughput against this code footprint, and the scalar byte-granular stores cap bandwidth at 27% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo peaks at 3.45 GB/s = 27% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling with 0% backend stalls and 48–53% frontend stalls, and the compiler emitted zero vector instructions (all scalar `vmulss`/`vaddss`/`vsubss`). The Halide branchless blend does not approach the streaming ceiling at any death rate or N; the scalar codegen and 379-instruction footprint leave the algo frontend-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.
